title: What ‘The Odyssey’ can teach us about economic policy
gist: Video page by Adam Tooze on what Homer's 'The Odyssey' can teach about economic policy; the captured text contains no transcript, only the headline and surrounding FP coverage of the expanding U.S.-Iran war and a possible Saudi-Emirati thaw.

insights.claim: Adam Tooze, director of the European Institute at Columbia University, uses 'The Odyssey' as a framing device for lessons on economic policy in an August 2026 Foreign Policy video.
insights.speaker: Adam Tooze
insights.so_what: Signals Tooze's ongoing narrative framing of policy choices; substantive content is not captured in the text.
insights.locator: What ‘The Odyssey’ can teach us about economic policy

insights.claim: Related Foreign Policy coverage argues the U.S. is learning the wrong lessons in Iran because tactical excellence cannot salvage strategic incompetence.
insights.speaker: Adam Tooze
insights.so_what: Military successes may not translate into a durable resolution, prolonging Gulf risk premia.
insights.quote: Tactical excellence can never salvage strategic incompetence.
insights.locator: The U.S. Is Learning the Wrong Lessons in Iran

insights.claim: U.S.-Saudi strikes in late July 2026 targeted a Popular Mobilization Forces base in Iraq's Diyala province, raising questions about whether the U.S.-Iran war is expanding.
insights.speaker: Adam Tooze
insights.so_what: Spillover into Iraq widens the conflict footprint and risk to regional oil infrastructure.
